application: Interactive fuzzy selector and command-line filtering utility

documented_platform_evidence.claim: The project documents Windows compatibility testing and terminal key behavior.
Upstream test matrix includes Linux, macOS, and Windows.

safe_execution_boundary.stdin: The runner launches the pinned sk.exe directly on the PTY. For deterministic fixtures, public SKIM_DEFAULT_COMMAND is set to the fixed case-local command `python emit.py`, which writes only items.txt bytes. No user value is interpolated.
safe_execution_boundary.environment: Owned HOME, configuration, history, cache and temporary paths; scrub inherited SKIM_* and shell variables.
disabled_features: commands other than the fixed fixture reader
safe_execution_boundary.processes: Skim is the direct PTY target. Its fixed fixture-reader child must exit after emitting bounded local data; Playtestr cleanup must prove the full process tree is stopped.

hooks.dependency_review: Reviewed 53 checksum-locked dependency build hooks; see dependency-hook-review-v1.json and active dependency-fetch-review.json.
hooks.executed: Executed as part of the pinned native Windows build; no target application run preceded dependency-hook review.

source_risks: Terminal event and redraw behavior depends on PTY dimensions and key encoding.
Selection output is written after interactive completion; an empty selection has a distinct exit status.
Interactive input may use a controlling terminal while candidates come from stdin.
Windows console and Unix pseudo-terminal behavior differ and require actual native evidence.

The normal no-stdin route uses SKIM_DEFAULT_COMMAND and launches a child shell. This campaign restricts it to a fixed Python script that reads only the owned fixture; other command, preview, IPC and history routes are excluded.
scope: Pins reviewed source/build boundary and the explicit feature-restricted route. No project admission is implied.
